text:
maya: Quick sync — we need to decide the internal API shape for the new routing policy feature. REST gateway or gRPC all the way? This affects console rollout UX and per-route quotas.

sam: My 2¢: gRPC internally for perf and typed proto contracts. But we keep a thin REST facade at the edge for browser/third-party clients.

ben: +1 on gRPC for runtime. But practical worry: telemetry & quota correlation if we terminate at gateway vs pass-through. If gateway terminates, we can count tokens/requests there easily. If pass-through, we need distributed accounting.

leah: Can we have hybrid? gateway terminates for public clients, but supports a passthrough header for trusted internal services. Gateway adds an `x-routing-mode: passthrough` flag so runtime sees original content.

maya: Hybrid sounds promising. Console UX needs consistent metrics regardless. We must show P50/P95 latency split by fronting protocol + model variant + routing-policy.

sam: Telemetry sampling becomes tricky. If runtime has the real latency, and gateway has fronting latency, we need to stitch traces. We should standardize a trace id header (like `x-rd-trace`). Envoy can forward it.

ben: For quotas: we need to charge token usage at a single place. My preference: authoritative accounting at the gateway for public clients; for passthrough/internal, runtime emits accounting events to a central collector (kafka -> billing). That keeps charges single-source.

leah: That implies we need a lightweight runtime accounting event: `{tenant_id, route, model, tokens, timestamp}`. We should sign events so gateway/billing can trust them.

maya: Agree. Also need a fallback policy: if billing collector is down, runtime should buffer and serve but mark traces with `billing:delayed`. Console should surface that.

sam: On the proto side — if we push gRPC, we should keep a single `InferenceService` proto and use HTTP transcoding at gateway for REST clients. That avoids duplicate contract logic.

ben: Example proto sketch: 
```proto
syntax = "proto3";
service InferenceService {
  rpc Generate(GenerateRequest) returns (GenerateResponse);
  rpc StreamGenerate(stream GenerateRequest) returns (stream GenerateResponse);
}
message GenerateRequest { string tenant_id = 1; string prompt = 2; map<string,string> routing = 3; }
```

leah: Nice. Console needs route metadata in responses so it can label traces. Maybe include `response.meta.routing_applied` with the policy name.

maya: UX for rollouts: when we canary a new routing policy, console should show a split-view: traffic % vs QoS metrics (latency, error rate, cost per token). We need rollout signals emitted by runtime for canary cohorts.

sam: Implementation idea: add a `rollout_cohort` header on requests when routing rules pick a canary path. The runtime includes cohort in telemetry and the billing events.

ben: Also add alerting: console should flag when canary cohort cost-per-token deviates > 20% or error rate > 1% relative to baseline.

leah: For quotas UI: customers want per-route quotas and tenant-wide quotas. We need a unified quota view that reconciles gateway-enforced hard limits and runtime soft limits (with warnings).

maya: Operationally, which component owns rate-limiter? Centralized at gateway (fast reject) + runtime soft guard. Gateway rejects early for untrusted or public traffic. Runtime enforces hard limits for dedicated/private infra where gateway might be bypassed.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout for `routing-v2` started in us-west-2 (20% traffic).

sam: One more concern — schema evolution for the proto. We must reserve fields and publish a lightweight compatibility guide for SDK teams. Also support HTTP clients with clear error mapping if a field is missing.

ben: TL;DR proposal:
- gRPC internal surface (single proto) + HTTP transcoding at gateway
- gateway = authoritative accounting for public traffic; runtime emits signed accounting events for passthrough/internal
- standardized trace header & rollout_cohort header for stitching telemetry
- console shows cohort split, cost, latency, and billing delay indicators
- gateway short-circuits rate limits; runtime enforces hard limits in private deployments

leah: I'm going to draft an RFC with the above and a sketched telemetry payload. Anyone want to be co-author?

maya: I'm in. sam?

sam: Happy to co-author and add proto versioning guidelines.

ben: I'll add quota-edge cases and billing event schema.

maya: Great — thanks. I'll open a PR for the RFC and link to this thread. :sparkles:

ops-bot: note: remember to tag the RFC with `team=eng-platform` and `area=telemetry` when publishing.
